newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Israeli officer jailed for refusing duty.
newsitem.headline: Israeli officer jailed for refusing duty.

text.p: An Israeli army officer was jailed for 18 days by a court martial on Tuesday for refusing to do reserve duty guarding Jewish settlements near the West Bank town of Hebron, military sources said.

"The responsibility for immoral acts falls not only on those who give the orders, but on those willing to take part in the occupation," state-run Israel Radio quoted First Lieutenant Roi Koslovsky as telling the military court.
Hundreds of reserve soldiers refused orders to serve in the then-occupied West Bank and Gaza Strip during the 1987-1993 Palestinian uprising.
But following the landmark 1993 Israel-PLO peace deal and subsequent troop withdrawals from both areas, refusal to serve on conscientious grounds was all but unknown.

Israel's long-delayed troop withdrawal from most of Hebron -- the last West Bank town still under occupation, and the only one with a Jewish settler population -- is at the crux of an impasse in peace talks between the Palestinians and the hardline government of Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu.
